title: Magnetic-texture winding controls fermion-parity switches in an interacting $p$-wave magnet wire
abstract: Coplanar magnetic spirals map locally onto uniform spin--orbit-coupled wires, but on a ring the rotating spin frame can change the electronic boundary condition. We prove, level by level in every fixed-particle-number sector, that even and odd texture windings impose boundary phases separated by half the single-electron flux period. Changing the winding by one also changes the physical pitch in inverse proportion to the circumference; a symmetric comparison removes this leading pitch correction. In the number-conserving topological phase, a global parity constraint then reverses the fermion-parity assignment of neighboring phase-winding branches. Density-matrix renormalization-group simulations show this reversal, support an Ising transition coexisting with a gapless charge mode, and relate the finite-size parity splitting to an independently calculated charge stiffness. Magnetic-texture winding thus changes the many-body spectrum through a global boundary condition that is not determined by the local band dispersion, providing a closed-geometry, number-conserving probe of topological pairing.
summary: This work analyzes an interacting p-wave magnet wire on a ring, showing that the magnetic texture winding imposes a global boundary condition. This topology dictates a switch in fermion parity between neighboring states, providing a robust, number-conserving probe of topological pairing mechanisms.
main_problem: The study investigates how the winding number of a magnetic texture controls fundamental fermion-parity switches within an interacting p-wave magnet wire geometry.
main_result: A global parity constraint causes neighboring phase-winding branches to reverse their fermion-parity assignment when the winding changes by one, demonstrating that the boundary condition is controlled by topology rather than local band structure.
method: The research employs a combination of exact fixed-number derivations and advanced numerical techniques like Density-Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG) simulations.
model_or_system: The system is an interacting p-wave magnet wire realized on a ring geometry, modeled by Hamiltonians incorporating hopping, attraction, and exchange coupling modulated by local spin textures.
key_observables: Signed parity splitting ($D_p(M)$), central charge ($c$) extracted from entanglement entropy, and finite-size curvatures ($ho_s$).
important_parameters: The winding number ($M$), the ring circumference ($L$), and the interaction strength parameters ($U, J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a fixed particle number sector and that the system can be mapped to low-energy theories involving charge and neutral Majorana modes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate pitch changes and parity sign reversals across adjacent textures; other figures show scaling behavior of energy splittings and entanglement entropy supporting critical transitions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the exact boundary condition imposed by magnetic winding to using DMRG simulations to observe parity reversal, followed by low-energy continuum analysis to characterize the nature of the quantum phase transition via central charge calculations.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete realization where geometric/topological constraints (magnetic texture) dictate global many-body properties (fermion parity), which is highly relevant for understanding topological superconductivity in engineered materials or superconducting circuits.
